project_specification.overview:
AutoForge SaaS Platform is the web-based control plane that turns AutoForge from a developer CLI tool into a fully managed service. Non-technical users visit autoforge.com, sign up, pick a tier, pay via Stripe, and receive a running AutoForge instance on Fly.io in under 60 seconds -- no terminal, SSH, or Docker required. The platform also adds three post-build DevOps agents (CI/CD pipeline generation, monitoring setup, and automated dependency maintenance) to AutoForge's existing agent system, closing the gap between "code that works locally" and "code that runs reliably in production."
The web platform is built on the Gen-Ai boilerplate (React 18 + Vite 6 + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Supabase + Stripe), which provides authentication, billing, admin dashboard, credit system, and email out of the box. The DevOps agents are additions to the existing AutoForge Python/FastAPI + React 19 codebase.

frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui and Radix UI
frontend.state_management: React hooks, context, and Supabase realtime subscriptions

backend.runtime: Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Edge Functions, Row-Level Security)
backend.database: Supabase Postgres (extends existing Gen-Ai boilerplate schema)
backend.billing: Stripe (subscriptions, one-time purchases, credit system -- already in boilerplate)
backend.hosting_api: Fly.io Machines API for user instance provisioning

autoforge_additions.database: SQLite with SQLAlchemy (existing AutoForge feature database)
autoforge_additions.frontend: React 19 with Vite 7 and Tailwind CSS v4 (existing AutoForge UI)

communication.api: RESTful endpoints + Supabase Edge Functions + WebSocket for real-time updates

prerequisites.environment_setup: - Node.js 18+ installed - npm package manager - Supabase project configured (Auth, Postgres, Edge Functions) - Stripe account with test and live API keys - Fly.io account with API token and organization - Resend account for transactional email - Gen-Ai boilerplate cloned as project base - Python 3.11+ (for AutoForge DevOps agent additions) - Claude Code CLI (for agent testing)

core_features.infrastructure: - System connects to Supabase Postgres and returns data from a test query - System applies all database migrations creating instances, instance_usage, billing_events, app_ideas, and builds tables - Data persists in Supabase Postgres across Edge Function restarts and redeployments - System contains no mock data patterns, in-memory stores, or hardcoded sample data - API endpoints query real Supabase Postgres via the Supabase client, not stubs
core_features.platform_foundation: - System loads Gen-Ai boilerplate with AutoForge branding and environment variables on initialization - System creates Row-Level Security policies enforcing user-scoped data access on all AutoForge tables - System creates database indexes on user_id, status, and created_at for all new tables - Landing page displays AutoForge hero section with value proposition and CTA button - Landing page displays feature grid with at least 6 feature cards - Landing page displays pricing table with three tiers (Starter, Pro, Agency) - Landing page displays FAQ accordion with at least 5 questions - Landing page displays footer with navigation links and social links - Navigation header shows "Launch AutoForge" CTA button linking to signup
core_features.instance_dashboard: - Authenticated user sees a protected dashboard with AutoForge branding - Dashboard displays instance status card showing current state (provisioning/running/suspended/destroyed) - Dashboard displays instance URL as a clickable link when instance is running - Dashboard displays current subscription tier with feature summary - Settings panel allows user to enter and save their Anthropic API key - Settings panel displays current API key mode (BYO or metered) with explanation - Settings panel displays credit balance and link to purchase more credits - Dashboard shows "No instance" empty state with CTA to start onboarding wizard - Dashboard shows degraded state message with retry when Fly.io API is unreachable
core_features.stripe_tier_configuration: - System configures Stripe products and prices for Starter, Pro, and Agency tiers - Pricing page displays tier comparison with features, credits, and VPS specs per tier - Pricing page links to Stripe checkout for each tier - checkout.session.completed webhook triggers Fly.io instance provisioning - invoice.payment_failed webhook initiates instance suspension flow - invoice.paid webhook triggers instance resume for previously suspended instances - customer.subscription.updated webhook handles tier upgrade and downgrade - Billing portal link in dashboard settings allows user to manage their subscription - Dashboard shows error toast with retry option when Stripe checkout fails or is cancelled
core_features.flyio_provisioning: - Edge Function creates a Fly app with unique name (autoforge-{userId}) on checkout completion - Edge Function creates a Fly Machine with Docker image and tier-based resource allocation - Edge Function attaches a Fly Volume for persistent project data storage - Edge Function sets environment variables (API key, tier, instance ID) on the Machine - Edge Function polls health endpoint with 90-second timeout until instance responds - Edge Function writes instance record to Supabase with status and URLs on success - Edge Function rolls back all created resources (Machine, Volume, app) on any provisioning failure - Edge Function sends welcome email with instance URL via Resend on successful provisioning - Dashboard shows error state with retry button when provisioning fails or times out - Dashboard shows provisioning progress with real-time status messages during creation
core_features.instance_lifecycle: - System sends warning email 3 days before suspending an instance on payment failure - System stops Fly Machine and sets instance status to suspended after grace period - System starts Fly Machine and restores running status when payment is received - System resizes Machine CPU and memory when user changes subscription tier - System sets instance to destroying status when user cancels subscription - System deletes Machine, Volume, and Fly app after 30-day destroy grace period - Dashboard displays current lifecycle status with appropriate messaging per state - Suspended instance shows "Update payment to resume" with link to billing portal - Destroying instance shows countdown to permanent deletion with reactivation option - Health monitoring periodically checks running instances and auto-restarts unresponsive ones
core_features.entitlements_api: - GET /api/entitlements returns user tier, credits remaining, max agents, and available components - GET /api/entitlements returns available boilerplates based on user tier - POST /api/credits/deduct validates credit balance and deducts credits for a build - POST /api/credits/deduct returns authorized:false with deficit amount when credits are insufficient - Insufficient credits response includes checkout URL for buying more credits - VPS and local AutoForge instances authenticate via JWT token against Supabase - Entitlements endpoint validates JWT and rejects expired or invalid tokens - Credit deduction is atomic -- no partial deductions on failure
core_features.custom_domains: - User can enter a custom domain in dashboard settings - System displays CNAME setup instructions with target hostname and copy button - System creates a TLS certificate via Fly.io Certificates API for the custom domain - System polls DNS propagation and displays verification status (pending/verified/active/error) - System updates instance URL to custom domain in Supabase after successful verification - Dashboard shows domain status badge next to the instance URL - Dashboard shows error message with troubleshooting steps when DNS verification fails - User can remove a custom domain and revert to the default autoforge.app URL
core_features.usage_tracking: - AutoForge instances report usage metrics (agent minutes, tokens, projects, features) to Edge Function - Edge Function validates and writes usage data to instance_usage table with daily rollup - Dashboard displays usage chart showing agent minutes over the past 30 days - Dashboard displays usage chart showing projects created and features built - Instance status card shows today's usage summary (minutes, tokens, features) - System sends overage alert email when metered key users approach token budget - Usage data aggregates correctly across date boundaries - System silently queues failed usage reports and retries on next reporting interval
core_features.onboarding_wizard: - Post-signup wizard displays multi-step flow with progress indicator - Step 1 allows user to choose API key mode (BYO vs metered) with explanations - Step 2 accepts Anthropic API key input and validates it against the Anthropic API - Step 2 shows validation result (success checkmark or error message) - Step 3 displays tier selection with feature comparison table - Step 4 connects to boilerplate Stripe checkout for the selected tier - Step 5 shows deploy animation with real-time status messages from provisioner - Step 6 displays "Your AutoForge is ready!" with clickable instance URL - Wizard sends welcome email via Resend on completion - User can exit and resume the wizard at any incomplete step - Wizard shows error message and retry option when API key validation fails - Wizard returns to payment step with explanation when Stripe checkout is cancelled
core_features.admin_dashboard: - Admin dashboard displays all instances table with status, tier, user email, and health - Admin can search and filter instances by status, tier, or user email - Admin dashboard displays revenue metrics cards (MRR, churn rate, ARPU) - Revenue metrics are calculated from billing_events table data - Admin can restart a user's instance via support tools panel - Admin can extend a user's destroy grace period - Admin can manually change a user's tier - Admin dashboard displays aggregate usage analytics from instance_usage table - Admin-only routes are protected with role-based access from boilerplate
core_features.landing_page_polish: - Landing page displays competitor comparison table (AutoForge vs Lovable vs Bolt vs Cursor) - Landing page displays testimonials section with placeholder content - Blog list page displays article cards with title, excerpt, and date - Blog detail page renders markdown content with syntax highlighting - Blog contains initial "What is AutoForge?" post - Blog contains initial "AutoForge vs Cursor" comparison post - Landing page includes title and description meta tags for SEO - Landing page includes Open Graph and Twitter card meta tags for social sharing - Product page includes JSON-LD structured data for search engines - System generates sitemap accessible at /sitemap.xml - Images use lazy loading and external resources use preconnect hints
core_features.app_ideas_system: - User can create an app idea with name, description, and target audience - User can view a list of all their app ideas with status badges - User can edit an app idea's details including features, design preferences, and boilerplate choice - User can mark an app idea as "ready to build" - User can delete an app idea with confirmation - App ideas list shows empty state with CTA when no ideas exist - Ideas created on web are visible in VPS/local AutoForge instances via shared Supabase - User can start a build from a "ready" idea, which deducts credits and links to builds table
core_features.build_tracking: - System records every build (VPS and local) in the builds table with status and credits consumed - Dashboard displays build history list with status, date, features total/passing, and credits used - Build history shows which idea spawned each build (if applicable) - Build detail view displays components used and boilerplate selected - Active builds show real-time progress (features_passing / features_total) - Failed builds display error context and retry option
core_features.cicd_pipeline_agent: - New agent type "cicd" is available via --agent-type cicd CLI flag - New --deployment-target flag accepts vercel, railway, flyio, aws, or docker - Agent auto-detects deployment target from project files when flag is not specified - CI/CD prompt template loads via standard fallback chain with deployment target injection - Agent generates .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint, type-check, and test steps - Agent generates .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml triggered on push to main - Agent generates .github/workflows/deploy-production.yml triggered on version tags - Agent generates .github/workflows/security.yml with weekly cron schedule - Agent generates Dockerfile with multi-stage build optimized for detected tech stack - Agent generates docker-compose.yml with app, database, and cache services - Agent generates .env.example documenting all environment variables found in codebase - Agent generates platform-specific deployment config (vercel.json, fly.toml, railway.toml, etc.) - CI/CD agent uses read-only feature MCP tools and has no Playwright access - Orchestrator spawns CI/CD agent after all features pass (post-build hook)
core_features.monitoring_setup_agent: - New agent type "monitoring" is available via --agent-type monitoring CLI flag - New --monitoring-features flag accepts comma-separated list (sentry, health, analytics, uptime, logging) - New --analytics-provider flag accepts plausible, posthog, or none - Monitoring prompt template loads via standard fallback chain with feature list injection - Agent adds Sentry error tracking to the frontend entry point with ErrorBoundary wrapper - Agent adds Sentry error tracking to the backend app with unhandled exception capture - Agent adds /api/health endpoint returning status, version, uptime, and component checks - Health endpoint checks database connectivity, memory usage, and disk usage - Health endpoint returns 200 when healthy and 503 when degraded - Agent adds structured JSON logging middleware to the request pipeline - Logging middleware records method, path, status, duration, and request ID per request - Logging redacts Authorization headers, cookies, and password fields - Agent generates uptime check script with webhook notification support - Monitoring agent uses read-only feature MCP tools and has no Playwright access - Orchestrator spawns monitoring agent in parallel with CI/CD agent after build completion
core_features.auto_update_agent: - New agent type "auto-update" is available via --agent-type auto-update CLI flag - New --update-strategy flag accepts conservative (default) or aggressive - New --dry-run flag runs audit without applying changes - Auto-update prompt template loads with strategy and date placeholders injected - Agent runs security audit and records vulnerability count by severity - Agent applies safe fixes respecting semver constraints in conservative mode - Agent updates to latest versions including major bumps in aggressive mode - Agent runs lint check after applying updates - Agent runs type-check after applying updates - Agent runs E2E tests after applying updates - Agent runs API tests after applying updates - Agent creates maintenance branch and PR with changelog when all tests pass - Agent rolls back all changes and creates GitHub issue when any test fails - Agent generates maintenance-report.md with summary, dependency table, audit results, and test results - Auto-update agent uses read-only feature MCP tools and has no Playwright access
core_features.maintenance_scheduling: - System accepts schedule_type field on schedule creation to distinguish agent runs from maintenance - System accepts update_strategy field on maintenance schedule creation - System stores maintenance run results including date, status, packages updated, vulnerabilities fixed, and PR/issue URLs - GET /api/projects/{name}/maintenance/history returns paginated maintenance run history - GET /api/projects/{name}/maintenance/next-run returns next scheduled maintenance date - POST /api/projects/{name}/maintenance/trigger manually starts a maintenance run - GET /api/projects/{name}/maintenance/report/{id} returns full maintenance report - Scheduler service spawns auto-update agent subprocess for maintenance schedules - Maintenance frequency presets (weekly, biweekly, monthly) map to cron expressions
core_features.devops_ui_integration: - Project view includes a Maintenance tab showing last run status and next scheduled run - Maintenance tab displays history table with date, status, packages updated, and PR link - Maintenance tab includes "Run Now" button for manual trigger - Maintenance tab includes schedule configuration (frequency, day, time, enable/disable) - History rows expand to show full maintenance report content - Settings modal includes deployment target dropdown for CI/CD agent - Settings modal includes monitoring feature checkboxes and analytics provider dropdown - Settings modal includes update strategy toggle (conservative/aggressive) - MaintenanceRun TypeScript type and API hooks are added to the UI codebase

tables.instances: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table (autoforge.com platform) - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id)) - fly_app_id (TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL) - fly_machine_id (TEXT) - fly_volume_id (TEXT) - instance_url (TEXT) - custom_domain (TEXT) - tier (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('starter', 'pro', 'agency')) - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'provisioning', CHECK IN ('provisioning', 'running', 'suspended', 'destroying', 'destroyed')) - stripe_subscription_id (TEXT) - api_key_mode (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'byo', CHECK IN ('byo', 'metered')) - region (TEXT DEFAULT 'iad') - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - suspended_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) - destroyed_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) INDEX: idx_instances_user_id ON instances(user_id) INDEX: idx_instances_status ON instances(status) RLS: Users can SELECT and UPDATE only their own rows
tables.instance_usage: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table (autoforge.com platform) - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - instance_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> instances(id) ON DELETE CASCADE) - date (DATE NOT NULL) - agent_minutes (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - api_tokens_used (BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - projects_created (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - features_built (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) UNIQUE(instance_id, date) RLS: Users can SELECT where instance_id belongs to their instance
tables.billing_events: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table (autoforge.com platform) - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id)) - instance_id (UUID, FOREIGN KEY -> instances(id)) - event_type (TEXT NOT NULL) - amount_cents (INTEGER) - stripe_event_id (TEXT UNIQUE) - metadata (JSONB DEFAULT '{}') - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) INDEX: idx_billing_events_user_id ON billing_events(user_id) INDEX: idx_billing_events_created_at ON billing_events(created_at) RLS: Users can SELECT only their own rows
tables.app_ideas: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table (shared across web, mobile, VPS, local) - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id)) - name (TEXT NOT NULL) - description (TEXT) - target_audience (TEXT) - features (JSONB DEFAULT '[]') - design_preferences (TEXT) - boilerplate_preference (TEXT) - prd_data (JSONB DEFAULT '{}') - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft', CHECK IN ('draft', 'ready', 'building', 'completed', 'archived')) - build_id (UUID, FOREIGN KEY -> builds(id)) - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) INDEX: idx_app_ideas_user_id ON app_ideas(user_id) INDEX: idx_app_ideas_status ON app_ideas(status) RLS: Users can full CRUD on their own rows
tables.builds: NOTE: Supabase Postgres table (tracks all builds across VPS and local) - id (UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()) - user_id (UUID NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY -> auth.users(id)) - idea_id (UUID, FOREIGN KEY -> app_ideas(id)) - instance_type (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('vps', 'local')) - instance_id (UUID, FOREIGN KEY -> instances(id)) - boilerplate_used (TEXT) - credits_consumed (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - components_used (JSONB DEFAULT '[]') - status (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'started', CHECK IN ('started', 'building', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled')) - features_total (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - features_passing (INTEGER DEFAULT 0) - created_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - updated_at (TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) - started_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) - completed_at (TIMESTAMPTZ) INDEX: idx_builds_user_id ON builds(user_id) INDEX: idx_builds_status ON builds(status) RLS: Users can SELECT their own rows
tables.maintenance_runs: NOTE: SQLite table in AutoForge's existing features.db (via SQLAlchemy) - id (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) - project_name (TEXT NOT NULL, INDEXED) - run_date (DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - status (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('success', 'failure', 'dry_run')) - strategy (TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK IN ('conservative', 'aggressive')) - packages_updated (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - vulnerabilities_fixed (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) - tests_passed (BOOLEAN) - pr_url (TEXT) - issue_url (TEXT) - report_path (TEXT) - duration_seconds (INTEGER) - error_message (TEXT) - created_at (DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - updated_at (DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
tables.schedules_extension: NOTE: Extends existing Schedule model in AutoForge's SQLAlchemy schema - schedule_type (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'agent', CHECK IN ('agent', 'maintenance')) - update_strategy (TEXT, CHECK IN ('conservative', 'aggressive'))

api_endpoints_summary.entitlements: - GET /api/entitlements (return user tier, credits, max agents, available components and boilerplates) - POST /api/credits/deduct (validate balance, deduct credits, return authorization result)
api_endpoints_summary.stripe_webhooks: - POST /api/webhooks/stripe (existing boilerplate handler extended with provisioning and lifecycle triggers)
api_endpoints_summary.app_ideas: - GET /api/ideas (list user ideas with pagination and status filter) - POST /api/ideas (create new idea) - GET /api/ideas/:id (get single idea) - PUT /api/ideas/:id (update idea details) - DELETE /api/ideas/:id (delete idea) - PATCH /api/ideas/:id/status (update idea status: draft, ready, building, completed, archived)
api_endpoints_summary.builds: - GET /api/builds (list user builds with pagination) - GET /api/builds/:id (get single build with progress details) - POST /api/builds (start a new build from an idea, deducts credits)
api_endpoints_summary.instances: - GET /api/instances (list user instances) - GET /api/instances/:id (get instance with status and usage summary) - PUT /api/instances/:id/domain (set custom domain) - POST /api/instances/:id/restart (trigger instance restart)
api_endpoints_summary.admin: - GET /api/admin/instances (list all instances with filters -- admin only) - GET /api/admin/metrics (MRR, churn, ARPU calculations -- admin only) - GET /api/admin/usage (aggregate usage analytics -- admin only) - POST /api/admin/instances/:id/restart (restart any instance -- admin only) - PUT /api/admin/instances/:id/grace-period (extend destroy grace period -- admin only) - PUT /api/admin/instances/:id/tier (manual tier change -- admin only)

ui_layout.web_platform: - Landing page: Hero section, feature grid, pricing table, competitor comparison, FAQ, footer - Auth pages: Login, signup, password reset (from Gen-Ai boilerplate) - Dashboard: Instance status card, credit balance, quick actions sidebar - Onboarding wizard: Multi-step modal overlay with progress indicator - Settings: API key, tier display, billing portal link, custom domain - App Ideas: List view with status badges, detail/edit view, create form - Build History: Table with status, progress, credits, expandable details - Admin: Instance management table, revenue metrics cards, support tools, usage analytics - Blog: Article list and individual post pages with markdown rendering
ui_layout.autoforge_ui_additions: - Maintenance tab in project view: Summary card, history table, schedule config, "Run Now" button - Maintenance report viewer: Expandable inline report with dependency table and test results - Settings modal additions: Deployment target dropdown, monitoring checkboxes, update strategy toggle

design_system.color_palette: NOTE: Gen-Ai boilerplate defaults -- customize with AutoForge branding - Primary: #6366F1 (indigo -- AutoForge brand) - Secondary: #8B5CF6 (violet -- accent) - Background: #FFFFFF (light), #0F172A (dark) - Text: #1E293B (light), #E2E8F0 (dark) - Error: #EF4444 - Success: #10B981 - Warning: #F59E0B - Muted: #64748B
design_system.typography: - Font family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif - Headings: font-bold - Body: font-normal - Code: JetBrains Mono, monospace
design_system.spacing: - Base unit: 4px (Tailwind default) - Card padding: p-6 (24px) - Section gap: gap-8 (32px) - Form field gap: gap-4 (16px) - Page max-width: max-w-7xl (1280px) centered
design_system.components: - Use shadcn/ui and Radix UI components from boilerplate - Consistent border-radius: rounded-lg (8px) - Consistent shadow: shadow-sm for cards, shadow-lg for modals - Button variants: default, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link

ui_ux_standards.banned_patterns: - alert(), confirm(), prompt() -- Use shadcn/ui Dialog and Toast instead - Text-only empty states -- Use EmptyState component with icon + CTA - Loading states that just say "Loading..." -- Use Skeleton components from shadcn/ui - Delete without confirmation -- Always use AlertDialog (shadcn/ui ConfirmModal equivalent) - Raw timestamps -- Format as relative time using date-fns or similar - Hardcoded API keys in source code -- Always use environment variables - Inline styles -- Tailwind utility classes only
ui_ux_standards.required_components: - Dialog (Modal), AlertDialog (ConfirmModal), Toast notification system - Skeleton loader, EmptyState with icon and CTA, ErrorBoundary - Button with loading spinner state, Avatar with fallback initials - Badge for status indicators, Progress bar for provisioning/build status
ui_ux_standards.page_patterns: - List View -> Detail View (read-only) -> Edit View - Never open directly into edit mode from a list - Separate view and edit concerns - Wizard flows use multi-step modal with back/next navigation
ui_ux_standards.feedback_protocol: - Success: toast + navigate. Error: toast + stay + keep data. - Delete: confirm dialog -> loading -> toast + redirect - Provisioning: real-time status messages via polling/WebSocket - Long operations: progress indicator with estimated status
ui_ux_standards.polish_requirements: - Relative dates, text truncation, back navigation, hover states, focus states - Autofocus first input in forms, search/filter on lists with 5+ items - Retry action on every error state, loading skeletons for async data
ui_ux_standards.accessibility_basics: - Focus rings on interactive elements, Escape closes dialogs - aria-labels on icon-only buttons, labels on all form inputs - Keyboard navigation through wizard steps

coding_standards.architecture: - Gen-Ai boilerplate conventions for web platform (component structure, Supabase client usage) - AutoForge conventions for DevOps agent additions (routers, services, hooks patterns) - One component per file, feature folders for grouping - Service layer: Supabase client calls in services/hooks, not UI components - TypeScript interfaces for all data types, no 'any' - Environment variables for all secrets and configuration - Edge Functions for server-side operations requiring secrets (Fly.io API token, Stripe keys)
coding_standards.routing: - Public routes: landing page, blog, pricing - Protected routes: dashboard, settings, ideas, builds (Supabase auth guard from boilerplate) - Admin routes: admin dashboard (role-based access from boilerplate) - 404 catch-all route
coding_standards.error_handling: - ErrorBoundary wraps entire app (already in boilerplate) - User-friendly error messages, not raw errors - Retry action on every error state - Graceful degradation when Fly.io API is unreachable - Webhook handlers return 200 even on internal errors (to prevent Stripe retries flooding)
coding_standards.security: - User API keys encrypted at rest (Supabase Vault or encrypted columns) - Each user instance fully isolated (separate Fly app and network) - Edge Functions validate requesting user owns the subscription before modifying resources - Rate limit provisioning requests to prevent abuse - Admin routes use server-side role verification, not just frontend guards - Stripe webhook signature verification on all webhook handlers - JWT validation on all entitlements API calls

key_interactions.signup_and_provision_flow: 1. User visits autoforge.com landing page 2. User clicks "Launch AutoForge" and signs up with email/password 3. Onboarding wizard appears: user selects BYO key mode and enters API key 4. User selects Pro tier and proceeds to Stripe checkout 5. Stripe checkout completes; webhook fires 6. Edge Function provisions Fly app, Machine, and Volume 7. Dashboard shows deploy animation with real-time status messages 8. Instance is ready at yourname.autoforge.app within 60 seconds 9. User clicks through to their running AutoForge instance
key_interactions.instance_suspend_and_resume_flow: 1. Stripe invoice.payment_failed webhook fires 2. System sends warning email: "Payment failed, instance suspends in 3 days" 3. After grace period, system stops Fly Machine 4. Dashboard shows "Suspended -- update payment to resume" 5. User updates payment method via billing portal 6. Stripe invoice.paid webhook fires 7. System starts Machine and polls health endpoint 8. Dashboard shows "Running" with "Welcome back" toast
key_interactions.auto_update_maintenance_flow: 1. Scheduler triggers auto-update agent for a project 2. Agent creates maintenance branch and runs security audit 3. Agent applies dependency updates per configured strategy 4. Agent runs lint, type-check, E2E tests, and API tests 5. All tests pass: agent commits, pushes, and creates PR 6. Maintenance tab shows success status with link to PR 7. If tests fail: agent rolls back, creates GitHub issue, notifies owner
key_interactions.cicd_generation_flow: 1. All project features pass QA (build complete) 2. Orchestrator spawns CI/CD pipeline generator agent 3. Agent reads project structure and detects tech stack 4. Agent generates GitHub Actions workflows, Dockerfile, docker-compose, and .env.example 5. Agent generates platform-specific deployment config based on detected target 6. Files are written to project; agent exits 7. User reviews generated CI/CD pipeline in their repository

step.title: Platform Foundation and Schema
step.tasks: - Clone Gen-Ai boilerplate and configure for AutoForge branding - Add instances, instance_usage, billing_events, app_ideas, and builds tables to Supabase - Configure Row-Level Security policies on all new tables - Create database indexes for performance - Customize landing page with hero, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer

step.title: Dashboard and Stripe Configuration
step.tasks: - Customize protected dashboard layout with instance status and settings - Configure Stripe products for three AutoForge tiers - Extend webhook handlers for provisioning and lifecycle triggers - Build API key input and tier display in settings

step.title: Fly.io Provisioning and Lifecycle
step.tasks: - Build provisioning Edge Function (create app, Machine, Volume, poll health) - Implement rollback logic for provisioning failures - Build lifecycle management (suspend, resume, upgrade, destroy) - Add health monitoring with periodic checks and auto-restart - Build Entitlements API for VPS/local instance authorization

step.title: Advanced Platform Features
step.tasks: - Build custom domain support with certificate provisioning - Build usage tracking and metering system - Build onboarding wizard with deploy animation - Build app ideas CRUD and build tracking - Extend admin dashboard with instance management and revenue metrics

step.title: Landing Page Polish
step.tasks: - Add competitor comparison table and testimonials section - Build blog with markdown rendering and initial posts - Add SEO meta tags, JSON-LD structured data, and sitemap - Optimize performance (lazy loading, preconnect hints)

step.title: DevOps Agents -- CI/CD and Monitoring

step.title: DevOps Agents -- Auto-Update and Maintenance
step.tasks: - Add auto-update agent type with strategy and dry-run flags - Create auto-update prompt template with branching workflow - Add MaintenanceRun model and extend Schedule model - Build maintenance API router with history, trigger, and report endpoints - Extend scheduler service with maintenance schedule support - Build Maintenance tab UI with history, schedule config, and report viewer

success_criteria.functionality: - Non-technical user can go from landing page to running AutoForge instance in under 2 minutes - Stripe checkout triggers automatic Fly.io provisioning with no manual intervention - Instance lifecycle (suspend, resume, upgrade, destroy) works correctly via webhooks - Entitlements API correctly authorizes VPS and local instances based on user tier and credits - CI/CD agent generates working GitHub Actions workflows for the detected tech stack - Monitoring agent adds Sentry, health endpoint, and structured logging without breaking existing code - Auto-update agent safely updates dependencies, creates PR on success, and rolls back on failure - Maintenance scheduling runs on configured frequency with correct cron expressions - All data flows correctly between web platform, VPS instances, and local installs via Supabase
success_criteria.user_experience: - Onboarding wizard guides users through setup with clear explanations at each step - Deploy animation provides real-time feedback during provisioning - Dashboard clearly communicates instance status with appropriate CTAs per state - Admin dashboard provides actionable metrics and efficient support tools - Maintenance tab clearly shows maintenance health at a glance - All pages responsive on mobile (375px), tablet (768px), desktop (1920px) - All actions provide immediate visual feedback via toasts and status updates
success_criteria.technical_quality: - Zero console errors in browser - All Supabase data protected by Row-Level Security policies - API keys encrypted at rest, never exposed in client-side code - Webhook handlers verify Stripe signatures and handle idempotency - Edge Functions include proper error handling and rollback logic - All generated CI/CD files use pinned action versions and never hardcode secrets - TypeScript strict mode with no 'any' types - Python passes ruff lint check, UI passes ESLint and TypeScript build
